title: Issue #1 — Georgia county roster in force on the campaign reference date
referenceDateBasis: CAMPAIGN_START_DAY in src/sim/calendar.ts (dayOf(1942, 2, 1)); GDD §3.2 historical boundary policy.
method: Filtered the Newberry Atlas of Historical County Boundaries Georgia Comprehensive Database (tab-delimited, from GA_AtlasHCB.zip, dataset published 2010-06-30) to county versions with START_N <= 19420201 and END_N >= 19420201; exactly 159 non-extinct counties with FIPS crosswalk codes result. Cross-checked against the 2020 Census county code list (159 rows, identical FIPS set) and src/data/georgia-counties.json (159 rows, identical FIPS set and names). Independently corroborated by the 1940 Census Volume I Georgia chapter, which states Table 3 covers "the 159 counties of Georgia".
fipsPolicy: modernFips is the current U.S. Census Bureau county FIPS code (2020 code list). It is a software crosswalk key only. FIPS codes were first published in the 1970s and are never claimed to have existed in 1942.
idPolicy: id is the canonical game identifier GA-<ModernNameWithoutSpaces>; repoId is the existing US-GA-<fips> key used by src/data/georgia-counties.json.

discrepancies.note: All 159 county names in force on 1942-02-01 are identical to the 2020 Census names and to src/data/georgia-counties.json (case-insensitive; Newberry stores names upper-case, e.g. DEKALB / MCDUFFIE). The only Georgia county renames in the Newberry record are pre-1862 (Cass to Bartow 1861-12-06; Kinchafoonee to Webster 1856-02-21; Randolph (original) to Jasper 1812-12-10; Sections the First to Fifth to Lee, Muscogee, Troup, Coweta, Carroll 1826-12-11).
